I know that the Prosecution that has within the 65 ter framework a list of witnesses, but experience, and I'm speaking according to my experience, shows that in this list some witnesses will not come for several reasons, possible reasons. I will not enter in the debate, but I know some witnesses will not come. And when I requested the Prosecution to give me the scheduling of these witnesses, I wanted to have a plan, a schedule which was realistic and not virtual. So I wanted the Prosecution to tell me, Well, this is what is going to take place. There will be 80 or 90 or a hundred witnesses, I don't know, but 100 per cent sure witnesses which it would surely call or 92 ter or 92 bis witnesses, in such a way that I would be in a position before the Pre-Trial Conference discuss the subject with my colleagues of the Bench, to tell them, Well, this is what the Prosecution intends to do. This general picture, I haven't got it. I requested the legal officer to remind the Prosecution about my request, and I still don't have the answers. Therefore, Mr. Seselj, you're talking about 108 or 109 witnesses, and I'm not in a position to answer anything to that because today I do not know exactly how many witnesses, viva voce witnesses, will be heard, how many 92 witnesses, or how many 92 bis with viva voce and the 92 ter witnesses will be called. What is the -- how many witnesses of 92 quater. So what is the general picture for the Prosecution's argument which it wants to show with these witnesses? Because when I do have the whole picture, then it will be very easy for me to say that this is a witness who is coming to give evidence on Seselj's men, and I will say then the Prosecution is providing four hours, five hours, six hours, I don't know. And there with the general plan I may say and propose to my colleagues that six hours may be too much. It should only be four hours because other witnesses will come. And in order to evaluate all this, I need to have a picture, a global picture, a sincere and true picture. And Mrs. Dahl, today, on the 27th of September, I'm still waiting for it. I'm still waiting, which means I mentioned a hundred hours like that without knowing exactly what the real figure would be. So I may understand -- I do understand that if there is an agreement between two parties on certain questions, maybe some witnesses won't come. Well, all the better. All the better. Maybe. I don't know. But at least what was really necessary, what I wished was to have a general picture from the Prosecution communicated to Mr. Seselj, and everybody would know what to do. So, Mrs. Dahl, do you wish to take the floor on this matter, because I have spoken on this matter many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have both spoken on this matter many times, and what I have said previously and will reiterate today is that our witness list and our estimate for time is realistic, not virtual. I'm sure that the Pre-Trial Judge is not intending to impugn the integrity of the Prosecution's filings in any way. I reiterated in response the request from Chambers for a line-up, an estimate of the order of proof that, without a firm trial date, we were not able to give reasonably accurate information upon which such important and critical decisions as to the amount of time for the presentation of the Prosecution's case. The Trial Chamber must ensure adequate time to see that justice is done in the presentation of the Prosecution case, and we will endeavour with this new trial date issued to give the information requested to allow for a proper preliminary assessment of the duration of the case. I would like to address the question of qualification of Defence associates. It is not possible to waive the requirement that accredited Defence associates be licensed and qualified. Defence lawyers play a vital and integral role in ensuring the integrity of the proceedings. That role should not be denigrated by accrediting unqualified individuals. It is unwise to allow such an assault on the dignity of this Tribunal. There cannot be the payment of funds from the international taxpayer to unqualified persons who are not licensed to give legal advice and carry with them no ethical obligations to either the accused or this Tribunal. Those ethical obligations are fundamental to safeguard fair play and the pursuit of justice. The Appeals Chamber decision of 11 September of this year in the Krajisnik case reached a contrary result on the question of payment to Defence associates for individuals who choose to represent themselves. Addressing the same legal question and reaching a contrary result, this Chamber's decision cannot be reconciled and must be reconsidered in light of the Appeals Chamber's decision in Krajisnik. I also want to address the question of standby counsel. It remains --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I stop you just now, Mrs. Dahl. The decision of the Appeals Chamber, I know it just as well as you do, and certainly better than you do. Secondly, I have been extremely clear. Never, ever will I reconsider the decision which I have made. Never. So there's no need even to talk about this, discuss this. Thirdly, you are for the moment stating untruths. You are talking about the integrity of the assistants of Mr. Seselj, but this problem has already been settled. Don't you know? Mr. Seselj had given three names of three individuals to the Registrar, and among these three names were the three names I mentioned to you. There was never any problem therefore, so don't come back by the back door to question this. For the Registry, there is no problem left. The only residual problem consists of knowing among the three which is the one who would be in charge of the question of the financial assistance. It has to be a barrister. Among the three, Mr. Jerkovic is a barrister. Therefore, on this matter, no problem. You are very able, but you did not answer the question I asked, and you know the Rules enable me also to sanction the Prosecution. I had told you this several times. I request the Prosecution to give me its own schedule for the witnesses in the trial, a sincere, candid, and truthful picture. And you're telling me that you can't because you don't know the date of the trial, but this has absolutely nothing to do with this. First of all, the date of the opening of the trial has already been fixed. It will start on the 6th of November, so there already we have a date. I may understand that the following dates for the beginning of the hearing of witnesses are not finally accepted or determined; but despite this, what prevents you from starting with a case, a date, an assumption, 1st December, 1st January, 1st February? Do tell me, "Here is the number of witnesses and the time I need." What prevents you from doing this? What prevents you? Now, you tell me that you think Judges are ridiculous and they don't understand. Tell me that you can't give this picture, the schedule, because you don't know the date of the beginning of the trial. This is totally impossible to understand. What I'm asking you is for a plan, a schedule in which you tell me how many witnesses you intend to call and for each witness how many hours will the evidence last, and that's all, but for the whole of the case, because the Chamber is going to determine the number of hours attributed. I am not a Judge who is in the hands of the Prosecution. I am strictly applying the Rules. The Rule says it is for the Chamber to determine the number of witnesses and the duration of their evidence. But in order to determine that, you have to supply elements. Months have gone by, and I have been requesting for months to get those, this information, these elements. If you don't supply it, well, so bad for you. The Chamber will be in a position to say that we requested and that they did not supply the information, and we will decide on a certain number of hours which will be fixed according to criteria which the Chamber will consider as pertinent, useful. While if you were giving the whole picture as requested and the time needed, Chamber would fix a duration and would be enlightened, would be apprised of these matters. And I see up to now you refuse to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond, please, briefly, because I reject the insinuation that we are not cooperating or providing the information that you request. We have provided a detailed estimate in our March 2000 filing concerning our witness list. It indicates the crime base, the nature of the testimony, the estimates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are not in March 2000. We are in September. We are the 27th of September, 2007. We are on the 27th September 2007. I need this list now because in a few days, in a few weeks, the Chamber is going to decide on the duration of each evidence, and I need this now.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I understand. The only thing that has changed is the calendar. We've given you our good faith estimates. We are reviewing them. I can tell you if we are going to drop witnesses, but you have already had the information in front of you and which you have computed a hundred hours. I am looking at how to fit the evidence into that, whether to cause aspects of the case to advance or recede. I am cognisant of Mr. Seselj's wish to cross-examine witnesses. We have the order from the Pre-Trial Judge to recapitulate our motions under 89(F), 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater. As a part of that exercise, we will refine the information that we have already given to Chambers, and I do not, frankly, see the point of recapitulating information that is already in front of the Chamber simply to place it in a different format. I wanted to give the Chamber a realistic estimate of witnesses' availability based on a calendar date, because I am concerned that if I say someone can come on December 14th and they can't, then I will be accused and sanctioned for giving you false information, and that would be an absurd result. I do not think that that is the direction that this Chamber is heading in. I want to do my very best to give you the best estimates. And when the inquiry was made to me regarding our line-up of witnesses, no order had been issued to set the case for trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know you're doing your best, but perhaps there is a misunderstanding. You have a list of witnesses which should have given evidence at the beginning of the trial a year ago, and the President of that Chamber at the time had fixed a duration which, of course, had consequences for the number of witnesses, indeed. Since then new elements have cropped up which you have yourself been apprised of, and the fundamental element here is that the Tribunal is going to start to open, whatever happens. Willy-nilly, it will begin, and it will open on the 6th of November. Now, who are the witnesses who are going to give evidence? Last time, the matter was discussed. I had told you that you have communicated some -- you had filed some motions. I thank you for those. You did very considerable work since your arrival, and I recognise that. I appreciate that. You furnished a list not with the name of the witnesses but of the categories of witnesses who would come, and you had started by indicating that you wanted first to have the witnesses who would speak on the reliability of the witnesses and according to the order of municipalities. I had told you that what I wanted was a change in the order of witnesses. I wanted to start first by the municipalities and then passing to the witnesses who would give evidence on Seselj's men, Arkan's men, and so on, and Arkan we would go to the gist of the subject, the heart of the subject, which is the liability of the accused so that things would be clear and not at all confused. I thought we were on the same wavelength. And starting from that point, since you already have your list, what prevents you from telling me now that for the first municipality, which you had intention to describe, I'm taking just at random now. Supposing you want to speak about Bosnia-Herzegovina and crimes committed in Mostar. I have witnesses, 89, 90, 91, 97, 98, 99. I'm giving figures. I don't know whether these witnesses are protected or not; but even if they are protected. I can mention figures which will cause no risk for anybody. Normally, according to what I have perused, because you do imagine that I'm working on all this, about Mostar I would therefore have seven witnesses, 97, 98, 99. I see that 94 is missing on the transcript now. What prevents you to tell me now that in Mostar you are going to call these witnesses. Maybe that in the lot 89 or 90 will be viva voce and the other 92 -- will be 92 ter. I don't know. I didn't go into these details. But then after, you were to tell me Vocin, 1, 2, 29, 33, and so on. And you present all this. So to come back to Mostar, on the seven witnesses, maybe two will give evidence viva voce or maybe three. I don't know. It's for you to tell me now and not to wait the beginning of the trial, and this is what I just fail to understand. I don't understand why today you are not in a position to give me this programme. Because if you tell me, "We are going to start with the Mostar municipality, 89, 90, 91," if you do your homework, and I think you are doing it well, you have probably made contact with 89, 91 witnesses to tell them, "Are you going to available," for instance, if we start with them in November." Maybe one of them may way, "I can't because I'm in hospital." Another one will say, "I'm travelling in South Africa." I understand such problems. But, again, one has to see matters in such a way that you can prepare matters, because if you don't, I don't see how you can -- I'm sure you've thought about all this. And all I am asking for, personally in the case of Mostar, among the seven witnesses, who will be giving evidence viva voce? Who will be 92 ter? Who will be quater? Who is 92 bis? And if three will be viva voce, you may tell me for 89, two hours; for 90 three hours; and for 91, thirty minutes, and you would do that for each and every one so we would have a sum. In fact, I have already made my sums by going by the list of the Orie Chamber. Therefore, I can tell you how much time is needed; but between the Orie Chamber and mine, many things have happened. So I don't have all these elements any more, and that's why I'm asking you to give me this general picture. Perhaps you misunderstood me, but this is what I was trying to explain to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: With the entry setting the order for the case of trial, I have more information available to me; yet, we still do not have a date -- a firm date for the commencement of evidence. I think it is realistic that we are taking the Chamber's request for information into our work plan to prepare for the presentation of evidence, and I am labouring to provide the information that you have requested to look at how to fit a great quantity of compelling evidence into an abbreviated trial schedule, particularly with a short week and a half day for presentation of evidence. I will continue to try to refine the information that was provided to the Chamber in March 2007. That list reflects a revision and a pruning of the prior witness list. We dropped more than two dozen witnesses. We will continue to look at how we can present the most compelling case with due regard to Mr. Seselj's desire to conduct an effective cross-examination and to prepare his defence against the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read the transcript and endeavour to understand that within a few days the Trial Chamber will have to set the duration; and in order to do so, well, we need to know who the witnesses of the Prosecution are, how long it is foreseen that they will testify. With regard to knowing exactly how and when you can bring X, Y, Z to The Hague, it's up to you. That's your realm. What I have to do is determine the time allotted, and you know this as well as I do. If the Trial Chamber determines a duration that you do not find adequate, you will request certification for appeal. The Appeals Chamber will have to hand down a ruling the Appeals Chamber will examine the issue and - I say this from experience - will look to see whether the Trial Chamber took into account all of the aspects, all the specific aspects, and did not -- whether there was any mistake in assessing all of the material. But in order to avoid such mistakes, I need to have really all the elements of information; otherwise, I can only take a decision has random. If you're not satisfied, it will be submitted to the Appeals Chamber, and the Appeals Chamber will sanction me for having made a mistake. And, of course, as any Judge, I don't wish to make a mistake, and so I'm concerned about these issues as of now. Ms. Dahl, you haven't been here so long. You don't know how Status Conferences took place in the past. They would last a couple of minutes. But as far as I'm concerned, some changes have been made. Reports were written on the topic, urging the Judges to play a more active role in the Status Conferences, and that's what I'm trying to do. I'm trying to deal with problems upstream, so that they don't arise during the trial. I'm trying to ask the Prosecution to submit to me all useful information that will make it possible for the Trial Chamber to be as effective as possible. I'm also trying to ensure a fair trial, the equality of arms. What can be said today? The accused knows that there are lists, but he has no idea which witnesses will testify viva voce or under 92 ter or 92 quater. He has no idea, even though he is defending himself all by himself with his associates.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is simply incorrect. He has our witness list, and he also has a copy of our submission regarding the order of our witnesses that we filed in response to your direction. More detail than that is not required under the Rules; and as best as I can, I will give you more detail, but I want to give you accurate information, not speculation. I certainly want to make sure that Mr. Seselj has fair notice about who's coming, when they're coming. And in the other cases, the trial teams have been requested to present their line-up a month in advance, two weeks in advance and things like that, so that the order of witnesses has some grounding in reality. The Chamber is unable to tell me today what courtroom we will be in and what date we are starting on. So for me to say that Mr. X, Mr. Y, or Ms. Z will be here is pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you. I am not able to tell you in what courtroom we will sit, nor can I tell you on what day we will sit. You're perfectly right. However, what I am certain of is that today I do not know the names of the first witnesses you intend to call. I simply don't know. And if I were in the position of the accused, well, how would I prepare myself? If the trial is supposed to start at the beginning of November, how am I to prepare my cross-examination? Of course, I know that there are lists of witnesses and so on, but I don't know who will be called first. Well, the same is true for the Trial Chamber. I don't know who will appear first. I don't know what your plan is. And you spoke about and month in advance. Well, it's not because some Judges go by certain rules that I have to apply the same rules. Each case is very specific, and there are significant differences among the different cases. This case is quite particular. The accused intends to ensure his own defence. There was a precedent, the Milosevic trial, but there was amicus curiae, and so on. So this is different, again. So wanting to ensure a fair trial and equality of arms or means, I want to make sure the accused have prior knowledge of the witnesses who shall be called, even if though we don't know exactly on what date. That's really just a secondly point, the date. What's important to know is who shall be called. Now, I don't want to belabour this point any further, but I wanted to take note --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to say something? Judge, I have to go back to the problem of the application of Rule 92 ter, 92 quater, because when you gave the floor to Mrs. Dahl on that issue, she moved on to another area and then she went off in a different direction. Rule 92 ter and Rule 92 quater were adopted in 2006. The indictment against me was raised in February 2003. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence nowhere expressly deal with the question of the retroactive application of one's own norms and standards. There's a legal void which has to be interpreted according to international law and according to the Statute of Rome and the permanent legal court which does not have voids of this kind. At Rule 51 -- or Article 51 of the Statute of Rome of the International Criminal Code in point 4, the second sentence reads: "Amendments and attachments on the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, as well as provisional rules, will not have a retroactive effect to the detriment of the individual under investigation or somebody who has been condemned or is undergoing legal proceedings." From this, I deduce that Rule 92 ter and 92 quater cannot be applied to my detriment in these legal proceedings, and nobody will convince me that it is not to my detriment. It is certainly to my detriment if I cannot attend the examination-in-chief and so on, and if somebody accepts the -- what the Prosecution wrote about these alleged witnesses. So I refer to this legal principle which has a firm basis on national and international basis, both in the continental and Anglo-Saxon systems. So don't provide rules and regulations against me which were adopted after the indictment was raised because then I have no safety in law. And I have to tell you something else. I consulted some -- the legal advisors and associates of Slobodan Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let's me try to address what you have just said. You are relying on customary law, as well as the provision of the ICC that does not allow, in terms of procedure, retroactive effect that could prejudice the rights of the accused. Well, let us think about this problem together, and it's a problem that I am quite familiar with because Rule 92 ter is, in fact -- well, I was one of the authors. Since the 13th of September, 1996, a procedure is provided for, 92 ter. It makes it possible to save time. Quite obviously, it's a procedure that allows us to save time. Why? Because, in truth, what happens? A witness comes viva voce. What does the Prosecutor do? The Prosecutor has his written statement and asks him questions in order for him to confirm his written statement. The Prosecutor stands, has the statement before him, asks questions following the order of the written statement. So based on that, why spend three hours asking questions that are already answered in the written statement? It makes more sense for the written statement to be handed to everyone and for the examination to be based on the statement. That's the first aspect of my answer. And, secondly, contrary to what you said in the Roman-Germanic systems, well, if there is an investigating judge, what does he do? He hears the statement, and the written statements are then part of the whole file or dossier. And so some witnesses will be called during the trial, but not all of the witnesses, just some of them. The written statements are already in the dossier, and there is no cross-examination in the Roman-Germanic tradition. And what is included in the dossier is admitted into evidence. And now as to Rule 92 quater, it is true that the provision only relates to the cases in the statement is that of a person who has died. I'm sure you're thinking of Mr. Babic. I'm sure that you have Mr. Babic in mind. And if -- well, the Prosecution may ask for the statement to be admitted, and you say this could prejudice my interests because I will not be able to cross-examine him. But I've already given you the answer. The Chamber can very well exclude such a statement because it has to do with your conduct. Now, I don't know what Mr. Babic said, but, quite obviously, he made a written statement that concerns you and the fact that he met with you, and you are not given the opportunity to challenge his statement, then, in fact, there could be prejudice to your interests. So that's what I have to say for the time being. And you've raised a completely new issue --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, you are quite right in interpreting the rules of the continental legal system. All witness statements from the investigation enter into the court files and records and are used in judgement, however, only in case the Defence attended the investigation and could then take part in the questioning of a witness. Here the Defence never took part anywhere. It is the Prosecutor that wrote the statement. They did not provide me a record of how the witness was questioned, so I could see that he was threatened, that he might be a suspect, and so on and so forth, and what they did to entice him, offering him protection, a job in a foreign country, refuge for his family, and so on. Here, they only provide me with the bare statement provided by the Prosecution, and then that alleged witness signed in English. The statement was read back to him by a translator, an interpreter, and whether this was read back correctly and precisely or not is a matter that is debatable. I was not able to be present when he was examined and questioned. I was not able to put a single question to him. And you have Rule 71 where statements are given which can be taken only if the Defence can take part in the questioning, in the case of depositions. And I consulted the legal advisors and associates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with what you say, but you say if someone is no longer here, he's deceased, well, then you cannot cross-examine him. But let's take a witness, X, who has died. I'm not citing any names here. The Prosecutor requests the admission of his statement, and you are opposed to such admission for the reasons you have just explained. Well, nothing prevents you then in your submissions from saying, "Witness X says that he saw me on the 4th of February, 1993," to take an example, "in a certain city." And, in your submission, you can say, "He's lying. I never saw him, in particular, or all the more so because on that date I wasn't in that city. I was, let's say, in Belgrade or elsewhere." And in a footnote, you can refer to another witness, Y, who could confirm that. So the contradictory debate can still take place, even on the basis of written documents, because in your submissions you can very well challenge the substance of the written statement, even if, as you say, the Prosecutor supervised the statement and had the witness sign it. Nothing prevents you from contradicting what is said in the written statement. So there is a contradictory debate even in that context, and then the Chamber will rule. So I'm not sure I understand or follow your arguments.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, take a look at the reply by the Prosecutor to a response to the accused with respect to a request to the statement of Milan Babic, and then you'll see all the problems that were encountered. The Prosecution never disclosed to me the testimony of Milan Babic in Martic, Milosevic, Krajisnik, and the other trials if he testified in some more. What the Prosecution says is that the public sessions at which Mr. Babic testified are accessible at the web site of the ICTY. That means I have to switch the internet, the web site on and read it in English. That's impossible. Transcripts from closed sessions in English can be provided to the accused if he tables a request for that, and then I'm given it in English, or they offer me audiotapes. You see that they are violating your ruling. They -- what they should have done is that they be introduced in -- that Milan Babic's statements be introduced in these files and records and to send them that way. And they've turned a deaf ear to your ruling. I don't know what Milan Babic spoke about. There's nothing bad he could have said about me, except to confirm the thesis about a joint -- the existence of a joint criminal enterprise and me taking part in it. That's a phrase that he might have uttered. But six Prosecution witnesses died in the meantime. None of them said anything special to me for to -- for me to be afraid of it, but the Prosecution must provide me with all their testimony in other trials on paper before I state my views about whether I accept it or not. And what I tried to explain to you a moment ago is this: I consulted the legal associates and advisors of Slobodan Milosevic and they expressed doubt, because during those trials there were many witnesses, as Geoffrey Nice said, pursuant to 92 bis and a half. They tried to introduce that practice before it was provided for in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and they expressed doubt and concern about the fact that witnesses whose testimony was taken in the files and records and answered in cross-examination had somebody to give them a ready-made answer which they heard through their headsets and uttered in the courtroom. The witness was whispered into their ears. So those are the doubts that the legal associates of Mr. Milosevic have. Now, what prevents them doing the same thing and applying the same technique and technology here? Who can prevent an OTP staff member to whisper the answers into the ear of witnesses that they are then going to utter in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you've mentioned two things. The second one seems quite extraordinary. I'll come back to it. As for the first, I'm sure Mrs. Dahl will be able to answer that. The transcripts regarding Mr. Babic, Mr. Seselj has said that he has not received them. I seem to have understood that the Prosecution is providing for their translation into B/C/S. Is that right, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, with regard to that aspect, you will receive them soon since they are being translated. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's the first time I hear of this, that the transcripts are being translated, because what I received from the OTP and you have too is this reply in point 6, or paragraph 6 as you referred to it. It says: "The fact that the accused must use the official transcripts -- the interpreter is telling to me slow down. "The fact that the accused must use the official transcripts in English does not mean that these court proceedings are unjust or that the accused has been prevented from formulating a response to a request or to prepare for trial. According to Article 21, paragraph 4 of the Statute, the accused is guaranteed the services of a translator free of charge, and he must have associates who know the language and be able to help him. Before he was accorded this right, the Registrar asked the accused to select persons who fulfilled basic conditions set out in Rule 44 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, including at least one person which in written form and orally can speak one of the two working languages of the International Tribunal." Do you know what that means? They are now telling me to use transcripts in English, once again; whereas, you guaranteed me the inviolable right of being provided with documents in the Serbian language. I have four or five other problems that I'd like to raise here during the Status Conference which I noted of a similar nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll come to those right away. Yes, Mrs. Dahl, you have a response?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, please, I'd like an opportunity to reply, because it is apparent that Mr. Seselj has misapprehended our reply because he's distorting what we said. What we said was that we are in the -- we are using due diligence to comply with the order to provide all prior testimony in the format that Mr. Seselj finds most accessible. I cannot fathom out of thin air hundreds of days of trial testimony. We have given priority to transcribing the testimony of living witnesses. Mr. Babic is dead today. I will hazard a guess that he will still be dead in three months. I want to make sure, as we said in our reply, that Mr. Seselj has an opportunity to supplement any opposition that he has to Mr. Babic's testimony when he gets the transcribed testimony, but I have to allocate resources in a way that is sensible, and I do not wish to engage in an academic debate. If he wants material faster, there are ways to give that material to Mr. Seselj that he has chosen not to use. I am in complete agreement with providing transcripts of testimony in the native language of the accused, and we are working as hard as we can to make that happen. I think it makes sense to make the record of transcripts in this Tribunal available in that format. But if he needs the information faster, he can use an interpreter. He can have a language qualified staff. He can listen to the audiotapes. So he is not disabled except by his own choice, and it concerns me because I gravely want the trial to be fair and to have Mr. Seselj fully informed and ready. I am working in the utmost of good faith to make that happen as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have any doubt with regard to your goodwill and good faith. And, Mr. Seselj, there's one thing that I mustn't forget to address. You spoke about the Milosevic trial, and you said you were concerned because you were told that when witnesses were testifying, in the Milosevic trial, things were being whispered to them, answers were being whispered to them via the headphones. This is extremely surprising to go me. It would mean that a sophisticated system had been set up which seems utterly unimaginable to me. So if that's been said to you, please ask those who have suggested these things to you to corroborate or to prove it. It would be extremely serious. It would mean that during hearings witnesses had been manipulated, which would be a huge scandal. So this is very surprising to me. When a witness appears before us, if he is examined in English, he hears the question in B/C/S via the headphones and he answers in his own language. So what you're suggesting is that -- well, first of all, there's the question in English that he hears, then someone at the same time would be giving him the answer, and then he gives this answer in his own language. From a technical standpoint, this does not seem very realistic to me. I have no idea who your sources are.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I will try to get a written statement from the legal advisor who expressed this suspicion. Until that time, I will not mention his name. Most of the witnesses who testified here testified in the Serbian language. Mr. Milosevic cross-examined in Serbian, and there was time for an answer to be whispered. I am only expressions suspicions. Whether we have material evidence is another matter. But whether one of the legal advisors will sign a statement stating that he suspected that throughout the proceedings, I believe he will. As for what Ms. Dahl has stated, she says that the transcripts will be disclosed to me in the Serbian language. You, erroneously, call it B/C/S. This is an insult to the Serbian language. There is only the Serbian language. There is no such language as B/C/S. But Madam Dahl has forgotten one thing. She expressly state that had she would deliver to me only the relevant parts of the transcripts not entire transcripts, but I don't want the relevant parts because it is not up to her to decide what is relevant. I have to decide what is relevant. I want them complete, just as they are on the record in English and in French. I want them complete in the Serbian language, not just excerpts. There have been attempts to foist only excerpts on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, on this question of a selective choice of relevant passages, do you have an answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Well, it seems that's a misunderstanding, because I agree with Mr. Seselj that he's entitled to complete witness statements, and I would not put myself in the position to make a judgement as to what's useful for him or not. We have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in filing the motion to select what is relevant to this case. We doesn't want to give the Chamber irrelevant material. But as far as the disclosure obligation of witness statements, he gets the whole thing. He can pick and choose what he considers to be relevant and material. I would like to respond to the suspicions that Mr. Seselj raised, and I would request that the Pre-Trial Judge give Mr. Seselj an instruction. Lawyers appearing before you are required to have a good faith basis for allegations or arguments that they may base in fact. I think it contaminates this proceeding to have unbridled and ungrounded suspicions and accusations hurled around the courtroom that detract from the dignity of the proceeding. It's absurd to consider that the Prosecution is going to be whispering into witness's ears the correct answer; and if Mr. Seselj can find someone who will say such a thing under oath, he should do that first before he brings the accusation. He must be instructed that he has the same obligations to act in good faith as if there was a lawyer speaking before him. I hearken back to my statements before about the dignified role that Defence counsel play in proceedings, and the absence of Defence counsel must not allow these proceedings to be turned into a forum for Mr. Seselj to spout his view of the facts without any basis in reality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, yes, sometimes you launch accusations against several without any evidence, and this creates a problem because, in so doing, you can say today it's night, while it is actually daylight. Now, you've just spoken about this question of witnesses who would have had whispered answers, and this is very serious. I suppose you realise, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am fully aware of all this, and I refer to it as a suspicion. I can bring proof that the legal advisors harboured that suspicion. However, it's illusory to ask me to provide material evidence that it did happen. I can't do that, but it's a fact that Mr. Milosevic's legal advisor suspected that this was going on. They harboured this suspicion, and they conveyed it to me. That is a fact, and you can call it whatever you like. I refer to it as a suspicion, and I am now burdened with this suspicion. I will try to get at least one legal advisor of Mr. Milosevic to provide me with a written statement that there did exist a suspicion that such things were happening. He's not saying that it did happen as a fact, but that they had these suspicions. They were sitting outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quickly, just before we break, I want to also talk about the e-court system. You have seen, Mr. Seselj. You have a monitor in front of you; and when you press a button, you may then see some documents which will appear on the monitor. When you press on the e-court button, you see then -- you can see no evidence. So there is no document for the moment. But when there is one, it will appear on the monitor. The system is the following: Defence, when it intends to -- Defence, when it intends during cross-examination to show to a witness a certain document, Defence let's the Registry have the documents and those documents are scanned; and then the accused, yourself in this case, you may, when Witness X, Y, Z would be there, "Witness, I am going to show you document D424," and then the document D424 will appear on the monitor, because you have given it to the Registry so that it can be scanned. My question is very simple: Do you intend to pass on to the Registry the documents which you would use during cross-examinations?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, by the 10th of October, I am planning to submit to the Registry about 10.000 pages of various documents. I have already submitted one of my books. I may need to submit another one and have it translated in full. That is what I will need. These documents have been sorted according to the general locations of the alleged crimes. There is a group of documents for Vojvodina, another for Vukovar, another for Zvornik, another for Sarajevo, and one for Herzegovina. The documents for Vukovar, for example, will contain statements of the bus drivers who will testify that the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party left for Belgrade before the crime in Ovcara occurred, for example; then we will have documents showing that the police investigated all possible cases of violations of law and order and attacks on people and property the area of Vojvodina; then there will be documents from the trials of the group tried in Belgrade for the crimes in Ovcara. This material alone has 4.000 pages. I have to submit this in full to the Court, and all of this has to be translated into English because this will show that I am not responsible for Vukovar in any way at all. Furthermore, there is the Zvornik group accused of crimes that happened in Zvornik in 1992, and I will submit to you the documents available in relation to this, and they have to be translated. As for Sarajevo, some persons are mentioned, and I will deliver several hundred documents to show that at the times certain alleged crimes took place they were not volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. As for Herzegovina, the chief alleged perpetrator, a man called Grahovac, I will bring written evidence that at the time he was not only a member of the Serbian Renewal Party, a rival party, a party hostile to mine, but that he was also in Nevesinje, a deputy in the municipality on behalf of that party. I have proof to show that this man was never a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party. This is the nature of the documents I will submit by the 10th of October. I need these documents for the cross-examination of witnesses of the Prosecution, for cross-examination of Prosecution expert witnesses, and I will need most of them for my personal testimony. If you give me a hundred days -- or rather, a hundred hours to present the Defence case, my testimony will take at least 40 hours. That's how I have planned it. About 40 hours will be taken up by me, about 40 by experts for the Defence, and 20 will be Defence witnesses, but that's just generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So I see broadly that your defence is structured, and I understand that you are going to send these documents on the 10th of October. So my very simple question: Among these documents, you said you had a document which shows that the volunteers left by coach for Belgrade and that they were not there where the events took place. So this document, I suppose there is a document, did you give it a number? Yes. Each document has a number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the documents will be classified according to crime base. The documents will be labelled Vukovar 1, Vukovar 2, Zvornik 1, Zvornik 2, and so on and so forth. My have legal advisors will sort this out very nicely, which is why they are now driving to The Hague rather of flying, because they have a vast quantity of documents to bring here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see matters are progressing or making some headway. Now, the other question is VHS cassettes that have to be given after each hearing. When there is a hearing, you receive after the hearing the cassette. It is a video, VHS cassette, which you can then play on your VHS to see the whole hearing. Very well. So the Registry told me that they are now passing to the DVD system rather than VHS, which means that anything which takes place in the courtroom will be on DVD. So you will have the DVD disk and you can put it in your machine and see the same things. Is that a problem for you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a danger inherent in that for me, Judge. I can accept this in principle. I usually task my legal advisors, because the Registry have shown that they can do this job very quickly, and I get the video cassettes on the very same day. I give them to my advisors and they organise the transcription of that. So they have everything on paper. When the proceedings begin, I will instruct them to always have someone present in The Hague to transcribe everything, because it's difficult for me to use recordings. I need paper. And, later on, I will submit everything in the Serbian language, because I will have to quote these documents in my appeal. I will not be able to quote in English or refer to video recordings because for a normal man that's beyond his capacity. So I will have everything referred to by page in the Serbian version transcribed from the recording, and the Registrar will be able to check whether the transcripts are correct. That's how I have organised my service, and I believe that this will operate well. So I can accept that, what you have suggested, provided I am not then swamped with documents and evidence and everything else on cassettes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... let you have the recording on the VHS cassette which is then transformed in a scanned DVD.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those recordings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, just for those recordings, only those recordings. Now we have break for 20 minutes, and we will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. We still have 50 minutes, so quickly. Mr. Seselj, concerning Mr. Jerkovic, I invite you to let the Registrar know that Mr. Jerkovic is a barrister, a member of the bar in his country. This would be sufficient in order to settle the problem. The second problem which concerned me was that when there will be a hearing, you're going to come to the hearing and you have your own exhibits, your own binders. So today I have come with three binders. This may be that you may come to a hearing with eight or ten binders. Since these binders are in your cell, they will have to be brought here. So I concern myself with this matter, and this might be what we could do: Your binders would be brought by a guard to the entrance of the detention unit; after which, they would be given to one of your assistants at a quarter past 8.00, for the hearing begins at 9.00, just to give the time to your assistant to arrive with the binders. And when the guard will, either in your presence or not, give the binders to your assistant, a receipt will be signed by your assistant, according to which he will have received the exhibits in question. After the hearing, those binders will be remitted by your assistant to the detention unit, and then a piece of paper will be given to him, a receipt, according to which he has given back those binders. Would you have some comments to make about this way of proceeding --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- about this method?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no comments to make to what you've just said, but I would have some other matters to raise, so please bear that in mind with respect to the time we have at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I give you the floor for those matters you want to talk about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I have to say that I have a great deal of problems in communicating with the Prosecution, and I must congratulate myself on having shown extra goodwill during the break. I accepted some 15 disks and videotapes because they guaranteed that they were indeed just videotapes, and I took them in electronic form. But I don't wish the Prosecution to draw the wrong conclusion on the basis of that and to think that they can in future provide with documents in the same format. Thus far the Prosecution has supplied me with exhibits up to number 2.500, along with numerous exceptions, I don't know the exact number, 2 or 300 exceptions of certain documents, the disclosure of which has been prolonged. If the trial begins on the 7th of November, then I consider that by the 7th of October they should be able to disclose all exhibits to me by that time, along with the names of protected witnesses according to your instructions that I received yesterday or the day before, where it says specifically which names must be disclosed a month before trial and others a month before the specific witness takes the stand. Now, Judge, if they fail to disclose all the names of the protected witnesses and exhibits, then you'll have to apply certain sanctions towards the Prosecution because that means that the start of trial will be delayed, through no fault of my own. Then there's another problem, the disclosure pursuant to Rule 68(i). They have just disclosed several documents, two or three, over the past few months, and there are 207.000 pages of them, which means that they will have to provide me with those documents at least a month before the trial. The Prosecutor sent me a code by which I can access their database. That code means nothing to me, and I won't be accessing their database at all, because it is their duty to provide me with the documents on the basis of Rule 68(i) in the Serbian language. It's the same duty as presenting exhibits, witness statements, Prosecution, and so on, because the OTP is an officer of international justice and he has the right to pursue perpetrators and prosecute them, perpetrators of alleged crimes, and to disclose potentially exculpatory material. So these are tasks of equal importance and the OTP cannot place the emphasis on one without providing the other. That's quite obviously what they will do because I will enter the legal proceedings and process without having been disclosed documents according to Rule 68. Now, among the exhibits that they have disclosed to me, a large number was exclusively in English. I wrote to Mrs. Dahl on the 24th of September, for example. I sent in a submission to her, stating exactly the number of the exhibits, between 2.000 and 2.500, which are exclusively in English, and there are 135 of those. I can give you a copy of this document if you wish to see it, and I have pinpointed those documents. They were documents exclusively provided in English, and I sent them back in a separate package, because otherwise I return everything that is in English. If I'm given the Serbian version, I return the documents in English, but these are documents that are exclusively in English. Next, they sent me an expert report by Ivan Grujic; allegedly sent, however, I don't see this expert report by this expert anywhere. Rather, in appendix A, there is something which is just a table of documents and nothing more than that. Appendix B, they say, the Prosecutor versus Slobodan Milosevic, such-and-such a trial, transcript pages such-and-such, and admitted in the Vukovar 3, the Vukovar troika. Now, where is that transcript? I have not received it. Then the transcript of the Prosecutor versus Mrksic, Appendix D, I haven't got that either. Appendix B, the Milosevic transcript. What does that mean? It means that they don't intend to send me the transcripts in Serbian at all from the questioning of Ivan Grujic as an expert witness in other proceedings, in other trials; nor do they make mention that I will be supplied with that document ever. I can't see that anywhere. So this is a document September me on the 20th of September and is dated the 14th of July, 2006; whereas, I've just received it. I received it on the 20th of September, which means just a few days ago, and it was signed by Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I don't have Ivan Grujic's expert report or the transcript of his testimony either. Furthermore, they sent me two documents without the main text, the basic text, just attachments; for example, attachment to Dr. Osman Kadic's expert report. It says attachment A, a description of Osman Kadic's report; whereas, I don't see the report anywhere. Attachment B, some documents, and then they provide two or three documents, but there is no Osman Kadic expert report among those documents, because I assume that it's on e-court in electronic format; nor do we have the transcripts of his testimony in other trials either. The Prosecution tabled a request for knowledge on the basis of Rule 94, judicial knowledge on the basis of 94, but I don't have the basic text, and it says, Attachment A. I do have attachment A, but I don't have the main text. And documents have been listed here. I have a list of documents but no actual documents. So which documents are they? There are no markings saying that I've already received them amongst the exhibits disclosed. So what is this? What does all this mean? There is no explanation as to why these documents are sent to the attention of, et cetera. Next --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't interrupt me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Dahl, perhaps you'd better answer now on a certain number of points.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I thought that might make it more efficient, so before we get too far ahead, I want to make sure the concerns are addressed. Taking the most recent first, the material that Mr. Seselj is discussing has been served on him by the Registry; and as he aware, we have been coordinating closely with Registry to ensure the provision of transcripts of testimony in the speaker's language. It's outside of CLSS's policy to make translations of transcripts; and so as a result, given the Registry's undertaking last year to provide material to Mr. Seselj in Serbian, we have been assisting with regard to transcripts that have been appended to our expert reports. Consequently, in an effort to provide information as soon as it's available to Mr. Seselj, I understand that the Registry has been serving on him incomplete filings; namely, giving him the report itself and what exists in the appropriate language. We have undertaken to provide the transcription of the Serbian testimony that is appended to the expert transcripts. With regard to exhibits, I just got Mr. Seselj's reply letters and most recent letters concerning the disclosure of our exhibits, and I consider those to be easily resolved in the ordinary course of our collaboration together. I don't think it's necessary to resort to judicial intervention. With regard to providing Mr. Seselj access to the Electronic Disclosure Suite, we have endeavoured to place him in the position that would be occupied by Defence counsel; namely, giving him access to the available collections of documents that may be relevant to his case. When we get search results for terms that he's indicated are material to his preparation of his defence, we want to make them available to him as quickly as possible. It took quite a bit of work to have a terminal installed at the UN detention unit and to make sure he has training available to him, and that courtesy -- or the facility has been extended to the other self-represented accused to make sure that they're not disadvantaged unnecessarily by virtue of having elected to self-represent. Material that falls within Rule 68(ii) will be provided in electronic form as required by the Rules, and we're fully cognisant of the obligation to provide in paper in Serbian documents that fall within Rule 68(i). There is no attempt to divert attention away from our obligations. To the contrary, we are fully discharging them. It's an overstatement to claim that there are some 207.000 exculpatory documents in our possession and that we're somehow defaulting on our obligation to disclose. That's simply untrue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I understood there was at least nearly 6.000 documents. Mr. Seselj, as well as myself, we have received something like 2.500. Mr. Seselj is expecting and waiting to receive the rest. First question: Precisely when will the rest be available? When will it be received? Secondly, how is it out of the 2.500 documents there are some documents whose numbers are 2.023 or 2.068 which are in English and have not been translated into his language? This is the first question I want to ask of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, in structuring the renumbered exhibit list, we thought it made sense to leave space in the event that additional documents were numbered after the original numbering exercise. As a consequence, exhibits beginning at 4.000 are the undated documents. It would seem that the numbering would be continuous, but in fact that would be incorrect. The chronologically ordered documents run from 1 to 2.876. We also then segregated the 65 ter exhibits beginning at 5.000. Those are simply the representatively case of the motions to admit written evidence of witness testimony. They are not going to be reprinted because they're already in the record, but we wanted to make sure there was no misunderstanding that if we move for their admission in evidence that fair notice has been given. Videos have a separate number. Those were disclosed today, and the remainder of the exhibits, 2.501 through 2.876 will be disclosed tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, as for the documents which are in English and not in B/C/S, when will he have them in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: As soon as they're available, Your Honour. When I receive information that he's gotten an incomplete set, we, of course, attend to it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, pursuant to our order, if the trial begins on the 6th of November, 30 days before that date, he has to have the list of those witnesses or protected witnesses; that is to say, the 6th of October. On the 6th of October, will you have disclosed that list to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: We are finalising a motion for reconsideration of our protective measures sought for specific witnesses based on updated information that we think provides a basis for extending the protective measures that we sought immediately. As with our motion for certification, we will seek to abate the trigger dates of the disclosure obligations pending disposition of the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So your motion for certification was rejected. I have, therefore, explained that you will always have the possibility to request measures if you have new elements, new grounds which will have appeared justifying the fact that the witness for which protection measures were refused should have those protection measures. Some new elements may appear which appeared after the decision was made, so those decisions are provisional. They may be re-examined with new grounds. So there's no reason to seize the Appeals Chamber about that. So that certification request has been denied.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: With respect to the witnesses for whom we are satisfied about the adequacy of the protective measures based on, of course, the current situation, we will make the required disclosures on the trigger dates. I would like, however, to have the firm trial date defined as the commencement of evidence in the case, because I think that is continent with the spirit of -- the idea of delayed disclosure which it is coincident with evidence rather than lawyer's opening statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Strictly speaking, in law, the Scheduling Order has indicated that the trial will start on the 6th of November; and that, on the 14th of November there, would then be the Prosecution's arguments. All this is already in writing, so you must take account of all that. As for the disclosure to the -- for the exculpatory exhibits, Mr. Seselj has already told us. What do you have to say about that? Didn't you hear? I repeat. Concerning the exculpatory exhibits, Mr. Seselj has said that he had some difficulties. He quoted the figure of some 2.000 exhibits which he doesn't have in his own language. So could you give us some information or get some information on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm wondering whether there is a problem with translation. We are not going to bring exculpatory exhibits. We are bringing inculpatory exhibits as our evidence in court. If there are documents that are exculpatory, we disclose them in paper and in Serbian. There are exhibits that we have withheld disclosure pending determination of our application for protective measures. We've given Mr. Seselj an index of all of those documents, and we have them ready, so that at the appropriate time, we can give him the packages consonant with the Chamber's decision on protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was speaking of exculpatory evidence, I was speaking of those that fall under 68(i), those that are to be disclosed to the accused. I believe that when you will meet many of these problems, we should normally find a solution, because as I listened to Mr. Seselj, he cited a whole series of documents in which there are missing documents in the annexes or annexes are referred to, but then the supporting material is not given to him and so on. He mentioned a number of cases. So, perhaps, in the administrative procedure, there are some hiccups. Normally, when you transmit this information, please verify that the text is available both in English and in B/C/S, and that all of the documents are submitted. Among those that you submitted to me, I just made a random check. I didn't want to look at them in details yet. Just at random, I took one binder, and I realised that there were some things lacking or there was one translation lacking, for example. Of course, this can happen quite often. I know there are also photocopies and so on. But as rule, when you communication these things, please verify that the texts are given in both languages to avoid such problems. Mr. Seselj, do you have other topics you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Judge. Madam Dahl is behaving as if in these five years the Prosecution has done nothing to search for potentially exculpatory evidence under Rule 68(i). Her predecessor, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, in an official material disclosed that there 207 pages of such material, which I rejected at the time because it was on CD rather than on paper, on hard copy. We discussed this at more than one occasion. At Status Conferences, you have received this material, you have seen what it is about but the Prosecution has said nothing about it. In a Prosecution motion for the Trial Chamber to re-examine the motion of the 4th of July, number 208, she personally wrote and signed, in footnote 28 on page 6: "If the Prosecution is required to print out all the material that the accused has rejected hitherto, which is estimated to be 400.000 pages, the costs will be more than 75.000 euros. I'm not interested in these 75.000 euros, but only in those 400.000 pages. From June up to now, I have received not even 20.000 pages, when one puts together all the exhibits delivered to me so far. I haven't had time to count them all because I'm spending most of my time separating out those which exist in Serbian from those which don't and looking for other areas of the Prosecution. So 400.000 pages, when I'm going to receive these? How am I going to embark on the proceedings before these are delivered to me before the trial? Why did Mrs. Dahl write this if they don't exist? So these are evidence that these pages exist, and now she's acting as if none of this exists. What am I to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Dahl, we've already discussed this previously, the 207.000 pages. I didn't know you had written a letter in which to some extent you recognise that there were hundreds of thousands of pages and they can't be translated because it would cost 75.000 euros which is what you've written apparently.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is -- this is a stale issue that has been settled previously by the Pre-Trial Judge. Mr. Seselj is taking out of context information that was presented to him and to the Pre-Trial Judge that was settled with accepting a pragmatic solution to conduct electronic searches on specified search terms. The Pre-Trial Judge directed Mr. Seselj to provide terms that he wanted searches conducted on. He has failed to do that. Mr. Seselj is failing to draw the necessary distinction between Rule 68(i) and Rule 68(ii). He is also failing to recognise or recall the problem we discussed before, which is that the disks that he rejected are not actually documents. They are electronic versions of search results, and the pragmatic solution was to run the searches again and determine which prong of the Rule the material falls under. We've undertaken that. It's not finished yet. We are also trying to get the case -- all of the exhibits in, all of the other things that he is wanting that we shall provide. It simply distorts the record to claim that there are 207.000 exculpatory documents that we're hiding from him. It's simply untrue. We are making available to him in electronic form the relevant collection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not getting a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is sorry. Can you hear the English booth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was saying, Mr. Seselj, that the issue has already been raised before us. The predecessor of Mrs. Dahl, Mrs. Hildegard, had written that letter mentioning 207.000 documents, but, in fact, she did not distinguish between 68(i) and 68(ii). During the last conference, I told you that in light of this problem - and I do not deny that there is a problem here - the best way to proceed would be for you to inform Mrs. Dahl for electronic research what are the topics and documents that are among those 207.000 that would be of interest to you, to inform Mrs. Dahl of which ones are of interest to you. Because, obviously, if there were really 207.000 documents that were exculpatory, then you wouldn't be here. You just wouldn't be accused at all. It wouldn't make sense. So, clearly, there is a problem with regard to the number of documents and the breakdown of those documents. So how can we some of this problem? It is virtually impossible to translate 207.000 documents. So I encourage Mrs. Dahl to look at all of this very closely and to disclose to you on paper and in your language everything that falls under 68(i). However, with regard to 68(ii), as I said, you must inform the Prosecution exactly what type of documents you are looking for in order to defend yourself; and with their search engine, they will be able to identify those specific documents, print them, and have them translated if they are not yet translated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: If I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mrs. Dahl, perhaps let us give the floor to Mr. Seselj first, and then you can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I know very well why I am here, and I am not confusing Rules 68(i) and 68(ii). That confusion is being foisted on me. According to Rule 68(i), the Prosecution has identified 207.000 pages of exculpatory material. Under Rule 68(ii) --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I agree with you. But when the Prosecutor said 207.000 in that letter, she did not distinguish between 68(i) and 68(ii). That is the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Judge, because the material under 68(ii) has not been identified by the Prosecution at all. There's no need for the Prosecution to identify it. They are giving me their database at my disposal, which contains several million documents. That's Rule 68(ii). Everything that the OTP has already identified as potentially exculpatory and the number of pages that they have calculated, all this falls under Rule 68(i). They cannot first identify the exculpatory material and then give it to me to search. That is quite illogical. 207.000 pages have been identified as potentially exculpatory. This is not material that has to be translated, because as you see, it's all in Serbian. They say B/C/S. It's all in Serbian. So all they have to do is switch on their printer and print this out, nothing more, and then deliver those 207.000 pages to me. These are documents they have already identified, and what is in their database is for me to identify. You have offered an easier solution, for me to identify the sort of document I'm interested in, but I will do this only after the 68(i) material has been disclosed to me, and then I will ask for additional material to be identified. But this falls under 68(i), and it's in Serbian. So there is no dispute here. Secondly, Ms. Dahl has not at all explained what happened to those 4.000 pages which I rejected --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 400.000 pages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpreted] -- which I rejected because they were either on CD or electronic form. They filed a motion which you denied, to clarify your decision on my motion to 81 concerning disclosure. They asked you to re-examine your decision, and you rejected their motion. And in that document, they admit to these 400.000 pages. So they find it more worthwhile to say that these pages do not exist, rather than have to print them out and deliver them to me. You say if there were 207.000 pages, I would not be indicted, but the reasons why I have been indicted are quite clear. Those 207.000 pages are not exculpatory evidence but potentially exculpatory evidence, and then I will select what I will use in the presentation of my case, but I have to see them all to decide what I can use and what I can't. Everything the OTP has concluded can be exculpatory for any reason has to be disclosed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Dahl, on the 9th of July, 2007, I handed down an order in this regard on this issue, and I believe the order has been translated. And I remind you of the solution that was suggested, and I also said that you must continue to use all possible means to discharge your obligations pursuant to Rule 68(i). I asked the accused to communicate key words to the Prosecution that he feels are necessary so that the Prosecution can discover more efficiently any exculpatory material that falls under 68(i). That being said, listening to Mr. Seselj, he says the 207.000 pages are in Serb, and, apparently, he don't have those pages. Could the Prosecution not simply print those documents and give them to him? That would already solve one of the problems since it's not an issue of translation. You just need to print them out. And, secondly, when you mentioned in your letter 400.000 pages, what are you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Let me take the last question first. You will recall we had a coloured chart that Mr. Seselj brought to court that had a total number of pages rejected by him in the course of disclosure. That was the, shall we say, worst case scenario if we were required to simply take all those electronic disks and convert them into paper. I would say that that's incorrect to do and not possible in any event, because we would be faced, of course, with the situation that he is then saying, "I've just been dumped on by 400.000 pages of unstructured documents without any index." Now, I want to address the next question which is that I will inquire as to the possibility of the printout of 207.000 documents. I will do some research, because obviously I don't have at my fingertips the exact memory of what that is, where it exists, and what difficulties would be involved. I want to make sure, on a third point, though, that the record is clear. Our giving Mr. Seselj access to the Electronic Disclosure Suite is not just giving him access to the evidence collection at large. We have prepared specific search results using the terms that he announced in court: For instance, White Eagles, Arkan's men, Yellow Wasps, and Vuk Draskovic. And using those, we've created a descriptive index of the documents. I'm going to give that to him in paper, so that he can then look through. He will have the document identification and what hopefully will be a useful short description, so that he can as at his leisure pick out what he wants to review. The beauty of having a small folder that he can select from is that it's instantly available. It's like having -- taking a trip to the library knowing what books you want to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's excellent what you have done. But, again, I'm a bit surprised, because on the basis of the terms that he gave to you, the White Eagles, Arkan's men, Yellow Wasps, and so on, you now have a chart. But for his defence, since Arkan is mentioned in the indictment, what he needs is the document that relates to Arkan or to the Yellow Wasps and the White Eagles. He needs that material. So why don't you just give him the document since you've identified the document. And it's quite obvious that those documents will be of interest to him because they're mentioned or those subjects are mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: They're not exculpatory, Your Honour. They don't fall within 68(i). They fall in 68(ii). They may be material to his preparation of his Defence. It is not possible to click and print on everything that he might find interesting. We will be here until next year when the doors close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mrs. Dahl, what do you know? How do you know that they are not possibly exculpatory material? How can you assert this? How do you know at the outset that it's not exculpatory material since he said to us last time that he challenges any connection with the White Eagles? That's what he said. So, since he challenges any connection, if there's a document, one might assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course, I don't know without reviewing them whether or not they're exculpatory. But under the general theory of the case, crimes committed by perpetrators who are tools of the joint criminal enterprise don't exculpate Mr. Seselj. We are exercising due diligence by bringing within our knowledge the information the Prosecution possesses, but I'm not a computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Dahl, I'm not going to get into legal aspects. You're quite right. However, don't forget that under 7(1), it's not only an issue of the joint criminal enterprise. There are other aspects as well, other issues, not just the joint criminal enterprise. So, if I've understood correctly, you will disclose to him the list of everything you've identified; and if he does request certain documents, you will give them to him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: No. We will disclose the list to him. If he wants us to print some of them, I will consider the request within our capacity; and if it's within our capacity, I'll do it as a courtesy, but I'm not a quick-print company. I am discharging my professional obligations to disclose pursuant to the orders of the Court. That is limited to material within our actual knowledge that exculpates him either for purposes of guilt or punishment. I am exercising due diligence in reviewing the material that comes to us. When we figure out something that could be Rule 68(i), we send it to him in paper and Serbian. That is the way this system works and his complaints are unfounded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, this part of the discussion has been very fruitful, because Madam Dahl has confirmed here that I am responsible for all the crimes committed by Arkan's men, the Yellow Wasps, White Eagles. She hasn't mentioned Vuk Draskovic's Serbian Guard, but it's mentioned both in the indictment and the supporting documents, because, according to her theory, we were all members of the joint criminal enterprise. She has now clarified before the public something very important. I can confirm now that I am being tried for what Arkan's men, the Yellow Wasps, the White Eagles, and Vuk Draskovic's Serbian Guard did. The volunteers of the Serb Radical Party are hardly ever mentioned. It always just says the Serb forces did this or that, and there were members of the Serb Radical Party, their volunteers, among them. Secondly, Madam Dahl doesn't want to work on finding exculpatory material under Rule 68(i). Look at the amount of such material that existed in other cases, and look at the amount that exists in this case. The discrepancy is astounding. I waive this right here now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
