utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you say look at all the documents disclosed in other cases regarding documents that fall within the scope of 68(i), but do you have any figures, because I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my knowledge, there's no case where there was not a hundred thousand pages of potentially exculpatory material. That's what I know about other cases. I've read mostly the judgements from other cases, but I have had opportunities to talk to other prisoners here in The Hague. I waive my right to have Madam Dahl discharge her duty as an international legal officer. She doesn't have to find a single potentially exculpatory document. All I ask is that those documents that Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff found, and she said she found 207.000 pages of potentially exculpatory documents, just give me those and don't look for any more. I'm not interested in anything more. Just give me that. But what is the problem? The problem is printing this out. They need 75.000 euros; not to translate them because it's all in Serbian, but simply to switch on the printer and use the paper. That will cost them 75.000 euros.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Dahl, unfortunately, I must bring this hearing to an end since there will be another hearing in this courtroom. I think one of the solutions would be to print out all of the documents that are in Serbian to begin with. Since there is no translation, that is necessary. It will perhaps -- there will, of course, be costs for the printing, but I think that's the best solution. Personally, I can't think of any other.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I will inquire, Your Honour, and I'll report back to you as to the feasibility of it, but I reject the notion that Mr. Seselj can waive having a fair trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We've taken note of that. Mr. Seselj, I have to bring this hearing to an end.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just two brief points, please, very briefly. Judge, I ask that you issue your approval for the Registry to deliver to me part of the tapes of the trial of Jadranko Prlic et al, where Counsel Karnavas mentioned my name and attacked me because of my words about him and his and behaviour at the Status Conference. I feel I have an objective right to have this delivered to me. Whether it's 15 minutes, 20 minutes, or half an hour, I ask that that part of the tape be handed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to that request, you need to file a written motion to the Prlic Trial Chamber. Although, I'm a member of that Chamber, it is the Chamber as a whole that must rule. So he need to draft a brief motion and submit it to the Trial Chamber in the Prlic case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in open session, so I thought it could be done without formalities. It was not in closed session. I thought it could be done quite simply through the Registry. But if you insist, I will file a written motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you have to file a motion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And one more issue I have to raise. At one of the previous Status Conferences, I explained a problem I'm having as regards my status as a detainee and my rights. I am the only one who for five years now has not been allowed to receive his personal friends as visitors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am quite aware. Indeed, your wife was supposed to come and visit you accompanied by the friend, and the friend of your wife was not granted a visa. This has been drawn my attention. It would seem from what I have been told that the friend of your wife had not responded to the requests made by the Embassy of the Netherlands, that requires since your country is not party to the Schengen Agreement, that some documents be submitted so that the visa could be granted. It's because she did not comply with this request to submit documents that she did not receive a visa. So, of course, when I learned of that, I was surprised and I tried to find out more because it's not appropriate that that visitors be forbidden to you, but it's simply due to a problem of the necessary documents. So this friend must submit the documents required by the embassy and then there will no longer be a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, they did not give you true information. The Registry approved the visit orally as they do in other cases. The tasks of submitting a visa request, a visa application, was done by my secretary from the Serb Radical Party. She's been doing that for years for members of my family. All the documents were submitted. Up to the very last day, they gave no reply. They just said, "We're waiting for the decision." And when the plane took off, I told the secretary to take back the passports and the applications. This is reliable information. They said neither yes nor no. They said nothing until the plane took off, and I did not receive a visit from my wife because of this either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What needs to be done is for your wife and her friend to quickly again address a request to the embassy to be granted a visa. I certainly do not have any opposition to this, on the contrary. And the detention unit and the Registry, well, it would also be in their interest for the detainees to be able to meet with those who are close to them. And if things continue to go on this way, then do not hesitate to write me a letter, and I will intervene with the Dutch authorities to settle the problem. Now I am compelled to bring this hearing to an end. I hope that I will find some time during the month of October for us to meet again before the Pre-Trial Conference. But if it cannot be set, then we will see each other again on the date of the Pre-Trial Conference, and I wish you all a very good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: at 1.48 p.m.
